base colour sRGB, colour variant "Silver" (shares N and ORM)

weights.method: rigid: every armour part is weighted 1.0 to one bone

rig.rest_pose: standing pose as modelled (not a T pose)
rig.animation: none: skeleton and skin weights only; no clips, no Physics Asset, no control rig
rig.skeleton: bespoke (CONVENTIONS.md section 11: any skeleton with a single root bone named root)

pivot: feet: armature origin on the ground between the feet, front on -Y
dresses: castle guard in full plate, 1.85 m, with a 2.3 m halberd in the right hand: sallet with pointed visor and bevor, globose cuirass, three-lame pauldrons and fauld, mail skirt, tassets, winged couters and poleyns, greaves, pointed sabatons; blue painted steel worn to bare metal
status: source delivered; not imported into Unreal, not bound to any placement
known_weaknesses: NOT photoreal at 1 m. The harness is forty clean swept solids: lames have no rolled edges, rivets, straps, buckles or hinges, the helm has a painted-dark sight and breaths rather than cut ones, and there are no fingers, only a mitten gauntlet. Nobody is inside: no arming doublet at the joints, no mail at the armpit or neck, so gaps between plates look into empty space when the limbs bend. The halberd is merged into the mesh on hand_r rather than delivered as a separate weapon with a grip socket. Rest pose is a standing guard pose with the arms down, not the A pose of the Manny skeleton, so retargeted clips need a pose offset. Rigid one-bone skinning (correct for plate, wrong for the mail skirt and belt). No animation clips, no Physics Asset. The red and silver sets recolour only the blue paint of the base colour map.
